newsitem.title: MEXICO: NAFTA nations to cut some tariffs from July 1.
newsitem.headline: NAFTA nations to cut some tariffs from July 1.

text.p: Mexico said Thursday it agreed in meetings with the U.S. and Canadian governments to remove some trade tariffs from July 1, the Trade Ministry said in the government's Official Gazette.

Under the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), the three nations agreed to gradually remove tariffs to facilitate trade. Private companies have requested a speedier removal of the tariffs on certain goods.
The acclerated tariff elimination on products resulted from an initial round of meetings between the three countries. A second round of consultations will be completed Dec. 15, the ministry said.

Some of the products on which the tariffs will be removed on imports to Mexico from both countries include: sodium cyanide, vitamin C, towels, ceramic dishware, tobacco drying machines and airplane seatbelts.
The nations removed tariffs reciprocally on some goods. The United States and Mexico agreed to remove tariffs on each others processed artichoke and stamped towels, for example.
The Trade Ministry listed close to 100 specific goods where tariffs will be eliminated from July 1.
